entries.title: Job 19:3
segments:
Ten times; many times, very often. 
 
The afflictions with which God visits us are greatly lessened, or increased, by the conduct of our friends.  If they are kind, and ready to assist us, they help us bear our burdens; but if unkind, negligent, and reproachful, they greatly increase our sorrows.

entries.title: Job 19:4
segments: Remaineth with myself; I must bear the consequences.

entries.title: Job 19:11
segments: No permanent or safe dependence can be placed upon the most intimate and endeared earthly friends.  For the continuance of their affection and care, we are dependent upon God; and if they are forsaken of him, they may forsake us.

entries.title: Job 19:14
segments: Have forgotten me; they neglected him, as if he were not remembered.

entries.title: Job 19:20
segments: With the skin of my teeth; but just escaped from death, or utter ruin.

entries.title: Job 19:22
segments: Are not satisfied with my flesh? he compares them to beasts of prey.

entries.title: Job 19:23
segments:
. 
 
  Printed; that is, inscribed, as the original word signifies.

entries.title: Job 19:24
segments:
With an iron pen; a sharp-pointed instrument of steel, such as was used to cut letters into metallic plates, or, as here, into stones. 
 
  And lead; after the letters had been cut deep into the stone, it was customary to fill them with lead.  The language of

, implies that what he is now about to utter is no common maxim, but a momentous truth, worthy to be perpetuated to the end of time.  By placing his words in the volume of inspiration, God has made them more permanent, and infinitely better known, than if they had been graven with a pen of iron and lead on the rocks of Arabia.

entries.title: Job 19:25
segments: Strong confidence in an almighty, ever-living Redeemer, and the expectation of meeting him as a friend and portion, support the soul in the deepest affliction, and cause it to rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

entries.title: Job 19:26
segments: After my skin; after my skin shall have been destroyed by the force of my disease.

Worms destroy this body; the words "worms" and "body" are not in the original, as the italic letters indicate.  The literal rendering is, "they destroy this," or, this be destroyed, meaning this body. 
 
  In my flesh; the literal rendering is, "from my flesh," or, "out of my flesh".  This is taken by some to mean, looking forth upon God from my body of flesh, that is, after its resurrection, which is the idea given by our version, "Yet in my flesh shall I see God."  Others understand the words to mean, seeing God when out of my flesh, or separated from my flesh, that is, in a disembodied state.

entries.title: Job 19:27
segments: Though my reins be consumed within me; "My reins within me are consumed with earnest desire for that day," is to be preferred.

entries.title: Job 19:29
segments:
The sword; of divine justice, for your unjust treatment of me. 
 
  Wrath; such unrighteous wrath as yours towards me. 
 
  A judgment; when God will reward all according to their works.
